subject.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)

question: Should OpenClaw accept runtime re-derivation for legacy no-pluginId/no-code diagnostics whose absolute source path is gone, or should that cleanup live in doctor/migration instead?
rationale: The explicit marker follows prior maintainer direction, but the legacy branch intentionally changes how upgraded persisted SQLite diagnostics are treated at Gateway startup.

options.title: Accept Bounded Runtime Invalidation
options.body: Keep the legacy branch, rebase, and merge once the exact current-main merge result is green because it unblocks upgraded users without manual SQLite cleanup.

options.title: Move Legacy Cleanup To Doctor
options.body: Remove the runtime legacy branch and handle pre-code rows through a doctor or migration-owned repair path instead.

options.title: Narrow To Explicit Marker Only
options.body: Land only the new diagnostic code and schema preservation, leaving legacy no-code persisted rows unresolved until a separate owner decision.

recommendation.title: Accept Bounded Runtime Invalidation
recommendation.body: Keep the legacy branch, rebase, and merge once the exact current-main merge result is green because it unblocks upgraded users without manual SQLite cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: They gave the predecessor's explicit-marker direction and have recent ownership signals in the plugin registry path.
